questions.text: Does SCRATCH read 0 right after reset, and is CTRL bit 0 also 0 without any INIT? (Scenario: After reset release, with no INIT issued and no writes, the host reads SCRATCH and then CTRL.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes to both. SCRATCH resets to 0 (register table: 'resets to 0'), and CTRL reads 0 after reset with no INIT, because bit 0 is self-clearing and CTRL resets to 0.
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What do the reads of 0x7F0 and SCRATCH return? (Scenario: The host writes 0xDEADBEEF to unmapped address 0x7F0, then reads address 0x7F0 and reads SCRATCH (previously 0x55).) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Reading 0x7F0 returns 0x00000000, because the write to an unmapped address is ignored. SCRATCH is unaffected by that write and still reads 0x55.
questions.evidence: Unmapped addresses read 0 and ignore writes.

questions.text: At T+3 and later, what does h_rdata hold: ID value, new addressed register, or 0? (Scenario: h_re is asserted at clock T for one clock only on the ID register (0x20930001), then h_addr changes to a different register at T+1 while h_re is low.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: h_rdata keeps showing the register that was addressed when h_re was pulsed, here the ID value 0x20930001. It does not switch to the register at the new h_addr, and it does not go to 0. The specification gives no duration for the hold beyond "hold it", and it says nothing about what ends the hold.
questions.evidence: After `h_re`, `h_rdata` must show the addressed register within 2 clocks and hold it.

questions.text: What value does BUSY_CYCLES read (is the tail counted as a cycle)? (Scenario: After INIT, 5 PUSH4 operations are done followed by one PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 2. BUSY_CYCLES is read.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BUSY_CYCLES reads 6. The tail push is counted, because a PUSH_N with N>0 is a processed push. The 5 PUSH4 pushes give 5 cycles and the PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 2 gives 1 more.
questions.evidence: - BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: Does the read return 0xA? (Scenario: h_we writes SCRATCH=0xA and in the very next clock h_re reads SCRATCH.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. The write takes effect in the clock after h_we, which is the clock of the h_re. So the read of SCRATCH returns 0xA.
questions.evidence: A write takes effect the clock after `h_we`.

questions.text: What is the resulting BYTE_COUNT? (Scenario: PUSH_N is issued with TAIL_LEN 4 (a value outside 0..3), wdata 0x01020304, after INIT.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BYTE_COUNT stays 0. Writing 4 to TAIL_LEN stores only bits 1:0, so TAIL_LEN becomes 0. PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN 0 pushes nothing, so BYTE_COUNT does not change and still reads 0 after INIT. It does not count as busy either.
questions.evidence: - PUSH4 consumes four bytes, least significant first; PUSH_N consumes the low TAIL_LEN bytes of the written word; with TAIL_LEN 0 it pushes nothing and BYTE_COUNT does not change. TAIL_LEN values above 3 cannot be written: the upper bits are ignored (only bits 1:0 are stored).

questions.text: Is BYTE_COUNT guaranteed to read 0 after reset release without INIT? (Scenario: rst asserts on the clock edge in which a PUSH4 of 0x12345678 is presented, after earlier pushes. After release, no INIT is issued and the host reads BYTE_COUNT.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. After reset BYTE_COUNT is 0, with no INIT needed. The specification gives the reset values for CRC state, BYTE_COUNT, BUSY_CYCLES, TAIL_LEN and CTRL. It does not describe a push that is presented in the same clock edge as rst, so nothing beyond the reset value is specified for that case.
questions.evidence: Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What does BYTE_COUNT read? (Scenario: BYTE_COUNT is 0xFFFFFFFC and one more PUSH4 is issued.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BYTE_COUNT wraps around as a 32-bit counter, so after the PUSH4 it reads 0x00000000.
